scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original independent B2 Plastic Ocean review-based test proposal pending human audit.

tabs.title: Film and Viewpoint
tabs.description: Evaluate how the reviewer presents the film.

tabs.title: Solutions and Limitations
tabs.description: Connect practical problems with the film's message.

tabs.title: Critical Review
tabs.description: Use the review to evaluate environmental arguments.

questions.q: Why does the reviewer describe the opening image as 'almost ridiculous'?
choices: It shows the concert hall before visitors arrive.
It gives an ordinary discarded cup unusually dramatic attention.
It tries to prove that the cleaners are responsible for all litter.
It shows a serious disaster caused by a single cup.
questions.explanation: Paragraph one turns an ordinary cup into a visual symbol, while questioning the film's reliance on images.

questions.q: What makes the street cleaner's conversation more effective than a shocking animal image?
choices: It allows the film to avoid discussing people.
It makes the beach look more beautiful.
It proves that disposable cups have been banned.
It connects the waste problem with specific decisions, timing and resources.
questions.explanation: The review values the cleaner's explanation of schedules, budgets and practical responsibility.

questions.q: How does filming the teenagers' chaotic preparation affect their portrayal?
choices: It treats imperfect effort seriously without making the young organisers look foolish.
It shows that they are dishonest about their event.
It suggests that improvising is more expensive than planning.
It presents them as experienced professionals with no problems.
questions.explanation: The reviewer praises the director for recording difficulties without mocking the teenagers.

questions.q: Why does the reviewer object to the film's treatment of reusable cups?
choices: It fails to mention that plastic cups can be coloured.
It suggests that security rules never affect visitors.
It understates the barriers faced by people in different situations.
It ignores how reusable cups are made from metal.
questions.explanation: The reviewer says personal responsibility is emphasised while practical constraints are brushed aside.

questions.q: What makes the deposit-system sequence unusually convincing to the reviewer?
choices: Every cup is reused immediately with no washing.
Organisers admit costs and uncertainties instead of presenting a flawless solution.
The system makes all packaging unnecessary.
It promises to remove every item of litter in the first year.
questions.explanation: The scene compares a proposal with its costs, losses and water consumption.

questions.q: Why does the first summer's higher cost not automatically prove the deposit system failed?
choices: Higher costs are always a sign of better cleaning.
Lost cups make the system completely free.
Organisers can ignore the cost of washing.
Repeated use may lower the price per cup over time.
questions.explanation: The review says the organisers expect costs to fall once cups are reused many times.

questions.q: Why would the reviewer prefer an ending about a meeting on bin collection?
choices: It would turn an appealing image into a discussion of who will maintain the solution.
It would make the film look less realistic.
It would remove all of the documentary's personal stories.
It would show that the coast cannot be cleaned.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph contrasts a beautiful clean shoreline with practical follow-through.

questions.q: A school film says that everyone can easily bring a reusable cup. What critical question should viewers ask?
choices: What colour should the cups be in the final scene?
How quickly can the film's music become more dramatic?
Are there rules or practical difficulties that make this harder for some people?
Which actor has the most lines?
questions.explanation: Paragraph four challenges universal claims about ease of reuse.

questions.q: Which lesson about documentary-making emerges from the cleaner interview?
choices: Only professional actors can explain environmental problems.
Emotional footage is always more reliable than any interview.
Showing schedules makes an environmental film less informative.
A strong explanation can show how everyday systems work, not only evoke emotion.
questions.explanation: The reviewer values practical details that give the problem a timetable and budget.

questions.q: Why are lost cups and washing water relevant to judging the proposed system?
choices: They determine which film scenes should be removed.
They affect whether the environmental and financial benefits are real.
They show how many teenagers came to the beach concert.
They prove that reuse always requires more plastic.
questions.explanation: The review identifies these measurements as necessary limits of the proposed solution.
